messages:
maria: Heads up — after the CUDA driver bump on h100-prod (driver 535.86 -> 540.12) we are seeing a 15-30% token-level latency regression for requests around seq_len=512. Autotuner seems to be picking a different attention kernel path for that length. Perf traces attached (nsys). :eyes:

deploy-bot: deploy: driver 540.12 applied to pool h100-prod-1 at 2026-06-12T09:15:00Z

sam: Which model/workload? stable across batches? any difference on A100 vs H100?

maria: Model: gpt-neoX-20b v3.1. Batch=4 typical. Regression reproduces reliably on h100 but A100 looks mostly unaffected. Sequence-dependent: small seqs (<=128) same; 512 is the worst.

raj: Can you paste the kernel-choice logs from the autotuner for a sample request? Also nv/cuda profiler outputs if you have them.

maria: Paste of kernel-selection snippet from runtime logs:

```
[2026-06-12T09:16:02Z] autotuner: seq_len=512, batch=4, hw=h100-sm_908, prev_pick=k_attn_v2_tile8 (lat=1.1ms)
[2026-06-12T09:16:02Z] autotuner: probe candidates: k_attn_v2_tile8, k_attn_generic, k_attn_tile4
[2026-06-12T09:16:02Z] autotuner: measured latencies: k_attn_v2_tile8=1.25ms, k_attn_generic=0.85ms, k_attn_tile4=1.30ms
[2026-06-12T09:16:02Z] autotuner: selected k_attn_generic (score=0.02, stable=0)
```

maria: Note the numbers — the autotuner incorrectly favors the generic kernel now. Previously it consistently picked k_attn_v2_tile8 for this bucket.

perf-bot: nsys summary: GPU kernel "attn_generic_kernel" dominated 62% of device time for those runs. Mean kernel time increased from 0.92ms -> 1.32ms for the attention stage (seq=512, batch=4).

liz: Do we see KV-cache behavior changes? Any extra memcpy or cache invalidations around the new driver?

maria: Good catch — KV cache hit path shows a new flush in logs after the driver bump:

```
kv_cache: policy=LAZY -> policy=STRICT_FLUSH (triggered by runtime-compat check)
kv_cache: flush_count += 1 (per-request)
```

maria: That per-request flush seems suspicious. If KV cache is flushing more often, larger effective compute occurs and kernel amortization shifts, which can change autotuner measurements.

raj: Hypothesis: driver changed some heuristics in cuBLAS/cuFFT or how shared memory occupancy is reported; autotuner's microbench harness is using a short window and the generic kernel shows better short-run latency but worse steady-state throughput. We need longer-run microbench to pick stable kernel.

sam: Short-term mitigation: can we pin the kernel selector for seq=512 to the previous pick? env override or force table?

maria: I tried forcing REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREFER=k_attn_v2_tile8 in the container and re-ran. Latency returned to expected baseline (median token latency down ~18% vs post-bump). Throughput slightly lower for other seq lengths but acceptable for canary.

ops-bot: Note: forcing kernel override is a config change that will be applied only to the canary pool. Use rollout flag --canary-only.

ci-bot: quick perf-run (canary) results:
- before-driver: median_token_ms=0.92
- after-driver: median_token_ms=1.15
- after-override: median_token_ms=0.95
(all for seq=512, batch=4)

sam: Good. Two parallel tracks: 1) rollback driver on affected h100 nodes if we can't find a safe runtime fix quickly; 2) make autotuner robust (sequence-length aware + longer microbench windows) and add a regression test to CI that checks kernel pick stability across drivers.

raj: Agreed. Action items I'm proposing:
- Add a feature flag to autotuner: min_measure_samples and stability_threshold. Default keeps short probe but enterprise builds enable longer probes. (ticket RW-INF-7123)
- Add arch-specific microbench harnesses (A100/H100) that run a 2-second steady-state kernel loop to estimate steady throughput instead of single-shot latency. (ticket RW-INF-7124)
- Fix KV cache compatibility check that toggled policy to STRICT_FLUSH on driver version >=540.x — that's a bug in the runtime compatibility layer. (ticket RW-INF-7125)

liz: Runbook for rollback if needed:
1) Place affected pool in maintenance mode: `redwoodctl pool drain h100-prod-1 --defer`
2) Roll driver to 535.86 via image `gpu-driver:v535.86` using our host-image rollback job
3) Run smoke perf-check: `perf-check --model gpt-neoX-20b --seq 512 --batch 4`
4) If stable, schedule full rollout rollback with change freeze window.

maria: I started a canary with kernel override on h100-canary-3. Early telemetry matches ci-bot numbers. Will keep it running and post more traces.

perf-bot: Also noticed kernel occupancy reports changed: sharedMemPerBlock reported lower by ~16% under new driver which could explain different kernel picks. Added to RW-INF-7124 as well.

sam: Timeline: if canary looks good by EOD, we will patch runtime (quick revert of STRICT_FLUSH and kernel-override table) and roll to prod. If not, we execute rollback runbook. Also add an automated alert when autotuner switches kernel for stable workloads (so we detect these drifts sooner).

maria: Thanks everyone. I'll keep logs and nsys traces in the ticket RW-INF-7125 and update here. :thumbsup:

liz: Filing incident ticket INC-2026-179 with rollback runbook and SLA impact estimate.

maria: Quick note: reproduction command for anyone who wants to run locally:
```
# run single-shot perf harness
./run_perf --model gpt-neoX-20b --seq 512 --batch 4 --warmup 10 --iter 200 --profile nsight
```

sam: :+1: follow up: add a unit test in runtime-autotune that simulates kvcache flush noise to ensure stable kernel selection.

maria: Ending updates for now; will post final resolution after canary completes (target 1834568540).

ops-bot: maintenance: h100-canary-3 set to canary policy at 2026-06-12T09:30:00Z

maria: (final) Canary passed — we will patch the runtime to avoid STRICT_FLUSH and land autotuner stability changes. Rolling driver rollback is on hold. Closing immediate incident, follow-ups in tickets RW-INF-7123/7124/7125. :white_check_mark:
